title: Thorn
imageAlt: Portrait of Thorn, a Veilguard and returned survivor
dek: A Veilguard member whose healing, field investigation and rebuilding continue after death and a hard-won recovery in Gael.

body:
Thorn dies during a husk hunt in Gael. The team is forced to leave the body. A cult later attempts to use Thorn in a ritual aimed at one of Gael’s Shards. By 8 September 2026, Thorn is alive and recovering at the Tower of Gael; she later appears alive in Prima on 19 September.

Recovery: the retrieved body, Ryvyt’s removal of the strange oil and Alyhotep’s Wish-based resurrection attempt now connect the stages. Thorn is subsequently alive; the precise spell-completion moment is not explicitly narrated in the recovered excerpt.

Belonging to the Veilguard

Thorn says, “I belong with the Veilguard, so I must return.” The wording establishes more than an assignment. By this point the Veilguard has become identity, obligation, and community.

Ordinary institutional life

Thorn also carries news of Farkur and the Ale-Chemy Knights’ disappearance, Ryvyt’s response, Gael transport, farms, and harvest work. A person who passed through death and cult ritual still participates in the mundane systems by which regions continue.

27 March 2026 · leading into The Before

Thorn leads the joint Pristinian–Rahuvian survey once the scholars arrive. She identifies the briars’ Delerium scent, bottles some of the purple haze for later study, and helps move the group through the changed entrance. The work places her at the boundary between field instinct and formal scholarship.

29 May 2026 · tracking through Howl

Thorn helps free and heal a deer caught in a bear trap, searches around the winter cabin, and later finds the wolf tracks that lead toward the den. Her contribution is not a single finishing blow. It is the sequence that turns a frightened wilderness scene into a route the party can follow.

10 October · restraint at the embassy

Thorn arrives in Pristinia through a Gate she credits to Adelia and says she came to check the farm and greenhouses. She joins the graffiti investigation, acknowledges her hatred of the Rahu after the war and nevertheless promises to behave while the party approaches the embassy.

The Dasa’s request brings her wartime memories into contact with people asking for freedom from their own hierarchy. The party departs with a promised search, without a completed liberation. Read the appeal.

Scene sources: 1, 2, 3, 4.

Belonging does not remove danger

Thorn’s later account of returning to Gael connects preparation with belonging: she will equip herself because she belongs with the Veilguard. Her reassurance that its members watch out for one another describes mutual responsibility, rather than a guarantee that nobody will be lost.

The recovered aftermath now supplies a means of attempted restoration: Alyhotep begins a Wish-based resurrection after the party retrieves her body. Her later living presence is established; the exact spell-completion moment remains unrecorded in the checked excerpt.

Magic that helps a harvest

Her plans to bless farmland belong beside the field work already in this history. They show an intention to support food production with nature magic; the plan is not a recorded yield or proof that the spell was performed. Tracking, healing and cultivation can all contribute to keeping a place habitable.

A connector in Gael’s daily life

Thorn describes the Ale-Chemy market and explains that she helps acquire things without being a Knight herself. Her account of Farkur and others having vanished remains attributed language. It does not establish death, disbanding or the cause of absence.

She also describes a trusted route for transporting known people to Gael. The testimony supports a social connection, not universal safe passage or a promise that travel now has no cost. Gael’s earlier restorers and continuing defenders remain part of the same history; no generational ranking replaces their quest-established work.

Recorded scenes

Dates refer to transcript postings.

    7–8 September 2026 · brought home

    Severina carries Thorn’s body back after the expedition finds it near Stake. The narrator describes it covered in strange oils and unguents. Ryvyt applies alchemical preparations; when they mix with what is already on the body, there is a brief flash and no oil remains. The party reaches the Tower of Gael.

    Severina asks Alyhotep whether he can bring Thorn back. He says he can use an arcane Wish to perform a normal resurrection and begins making that Wish without material components. This is a recorded attempt, beyond the earlier general hope of recovering her.

    By 8 September, Thorn is moving about the Tower and asks for warm tea in a low, scratchy voice. Alyhotep asks whether she needs more healing. These later scenes establish her living recovery. They do not supply a separate narrator description of the precise moment the Wish completes.

    September · returning does not mean being well

    The Tower conversation continues after Thorn first appears alive. She asks for tea in a scratchy voice, describes feeling dreadful and tells the others she died. Farkur greets her with relief and later offers somewhere she can rest, saying there is no shame in needing it.

    This strengthens the record of her living recovery and its physical aftermath. It does not supply the missing narrator description of Alyhotep’s spell completing, and her weakness is not turned into a universal rule about every resurrection. Returning to the community includes being allowed time to recover.

    Scenes in sequence

    Selected scenes keep the knowledge available at each stage distinct from later discoveries. Dates identify source postings in UTC.

    1. 2026-09-07 · checked scenes

      The body is brought home

      Severina retrieves Thorn’s body; Ryvyt’s alchemical treatment removes the strange oil, and the party reaches the Tower.

      Known at this stage
      Recovery of the body is established while revival remains ahead.
      Consequence
      The party obtains a body on which restoration can be attempted.
      Still unresolved
      Removing the oil is not itself a resurrection.

      Receipt 1 · Receipt 2 · Receipt 3

    2. 2026-09-07 → 2026-09-08 · checked scenes

      An attempted restoration and a living recovery

      Alyhotep begins a Wish-based resurrection after Severina’s request. Thorn is alive and moving about the Tower by 8 September; Alyhotep asks about further healing.

      Known at this stage
      The attempt and subsequent living presence are recorded at different stages.
      Consequence
      Her later Veilguard belonging follows a concrete recovery effort.
      Still unresolved
      The precise moment of spell completion has no separate narrator confirmation in the checked excerpt.

      Receipt 1 · Receipt 2 · Receipt 3 · Receipt 4

    3. 2026-09-08 · compatible RP

      Being back is not the same as being well

      Thorn asks for tea, says she died and describes feeling unwell; Farkur offers her rest.

      Known at this stage
      She is alive and conversing after the recorded Wish-based attempt.
      Consequence
      Recovery includes practical care and permission to stop.
      Still unresolved
      This later scene does not narrate the exact spell-completion moment.

profile.personality: Thorn is a field leader who treats belonging as an obligation: the Veilguard is not merely an assignment but the community to which she must return. She combines instinctive caution with practical curiosity, gathering evidence without pretending that every contaminated sign already has an explanation.
profile.achievements: A Veilguard member whose work in healing, field investigation and rebuilding continues alongside an unresolved history of death and return.
profile.relationships: The Veilguard anchors Thorn’s sense of self. Lady Severina, Miri, and the Rahuvian scholars share her survey work, while Minerva and Jéane Rose help transform the Howl clues into action. Thorn also carries news of Farkur’s disappearance and Ryvyt’s grief, showing that a returned survivor still participates in the ordinary work of remembering other people’s losses.
